title: Logic relocation ended in an eight-hour essential-sounds download
observation: After using Logic's relocation command, the poster still could not use the external library and was offered a new essential-sounds download estimated at eight hours.
product_implication: Treat a relocated library as owner-managed state; verify that Logic can locate and read it before the original copy becomes reviewable.
quality_note: First-person report with peer troubleshooting. It shows failure and uncertainty, not a universal Logic defect.

title: Logic library relocation competes with Time Machine use
observation: The poster wanted to reuse a partitioned external disk for Logic while another partition held Time Machine data and sought confirmation before setup; replies also described temporary internal download space.
product_implication: Show volume roles and temporary source-volume requirements before proposing relocation; do not merge backup and working-library actions.
quality_note: First-person planning question with peer replies. Version-specific details require owner documentation before implementation.

title: Partial Logic downloads left content split across drives
observation: With about 20 GB free, the poster downloaded and moved Logic content in chunks, then found the relocation destination unavailable while content existed on both drives.
product_implication: Represent partial owner transactions and split state explicitly; route continuation or repair through Logic instead of treating either copy as an orphan.
quality_note: First-person report with a successful peer workaround. The workaround is not promoted as an owner rule.

title: One external Logic library was not automatically reusable on a second Mac
observation: A second Mac saw sound-library files on an external drive but both location choices were disabled, leading the user to consider manual symbolic links.
product_implication: Do not infer that a library on a mounted disk is valid for every device; surface owner identity and compatibility before labeling duplicates.
quality_note: First-person report with peer workarounds. Current Logic 12 behavior differs and must be checked against first-party documentation.

title: Logic relocation was disabled by a Time Machine role
observation: The poster could not select an external destination and later linked the block to the disk's Time Machine role.
product_implication: Explain the owner-level blocker and offer a supported owner action; never suggest deleting backup metadata to make a destination eligible.
quality_note: First-person report with peer remedies. Destructive peer advice is evidence of risk, not a safe instruction.

title: Logic content needed more internal working space than its final destination
observation: A user with about 14 GB free could not complete a large sound-library install even after planning an external destination because installation packages first occupied the system drive.
product_implication: Budget download, unpack, validation, and final bytes separately and suggest owner-supported chunking when the transaction cannot fit.
quality_note: First-person report with peer explanation. Exact multipliers are version-dependent.

title: Logic lost a relocated library after the external disk was disconnected
observation: The poster's 49.5 GB library remained on the SSD, but Logic offered to download it again after travel and reconnection.
product_implication: When owner state is missing, prefer locate, remount, and verify over redownload or duplicate cleanup.
quality_note: First-person 2025 report with current-looking peer guidance; owner documentation remains authoritative.

title: Logic 12 still required internal space for an external library update
observation: A Logic 12 user reported that content updates failed an internal free-space check although the library and ample capacity were on an APFS external SSD.
product_implication: Show which volume each transaction phase uses and distinguish final placement from temporary working space.
quality_note: First-person report from a recent version. It is a reported behavior, not confirmed product specification.

title: The wrong external disk caused Logic content to return to the Mac
observation: The user connected a backup disk instead of the sound-library disk, approved a download, and later found Logic storing content locally with relocation choices disabled.
product_implication: Show the expected volume identity and the consequence of reset or download choices before any cleanup action.
quality_note: First-person report with peer repair advice. It supports better state explanation, not an automatic fix.

title: Logic relocation failed despite permissions and 300 GB free
observation: Relocating 1.43 GB failed even with reported full-disk access and more than 300 GB free on the destination.
product_implication: A size-only recommendation is insufficient; capture owner error state, permissions, format, and exact retry proof.
quality_note: First-person report with an incomplete troubleshooting trail.

title: Logic redownloaded sounds locally after losing an external reference
observation: The user had about 70 percent of the library externally, then Logic stopped resolving it and began a local redownload while an external copy still existed.
product_implication: Detect owner-recognized versus merely present copies and avoid duplicate classification until Logic confirms the active location.
quality_note: First-person report with peer symbolic-link repair. Manual filesystem work is not a default Tessera action.

title: A moved Logic library became unavailable despite the disk being present
observation: After a successful move, Logic reported that the sound-library directory could not be found while the Mac still saw the external disk.
product_implication: Separate device presence, path validity, and owner recognition; require an owner-level open test after relocation.
quality_note: First-person report with peer repair steps from an older Logic version.

title: Sample libraries remained the problem after ordinary cleanup
observation: A producer with about 30 GB free found that sample libraries, not ordinary projects or documents, dominated a 500 GB Mac and asked what could safely move.
product_implication: Group storage by owner and role, then offer supported relocation instead of ranking all large folders as deletion candidates.
quality_note: First-person forum report. Library sizes and performance advice are configuration-specific.

title: An Ableton upgrade raised compatibility and relocation anxiety
observation: Before upgrading, the poster backed up projects and asked which Packs, User Library, projects, plug-ins, temporary files, and cache could move without breaking references.
product_implication: Model each component separately and show both relocation support and compatibility risk before an upgrade.
quality_note: First-person plan with peer setups. It shows the decision burden, not one correct folder layout.

title: Ableton could use an external library but still needed installation room
observation: A user lacked room for initial installation while peers described keeping a very small local Ableton folder and about 50 GB of content externally.
product_implication: Plan the transition transaction, not only the final layout; show minimum local working space and supported owner paths.
quality_note: First-person report with peer configuration examples from an older Live version.

title: A dedicated external Ableton system traded capacity for speed and identity complexity
observation: The poster considered booting a music system from a 2 TB external SSD because a 256 GB internal disk was too small, while peers warned about performance and path placement.
product_implication: Show relocation benefit together with speed, availability, and device-identity costs.
quality_note: First-person planning discussion. It supports trade-off display, not a boot-volume recommendation.

title: An external Ableton working set still had performance and rollback constraints
observation: A user kept Packs, User Library, Sets, and other content externally to protect internal headroom, but external-drive health and cross-version project behavior still affected live work.
product_implication: Do not recommend moving an active working set based on bytes alone; show performance, health, and rollback constraints.
quality_note: First-person troubleshooting thread. Performance causes are not isolated.

title: Ableton library growth mixed duplicates, old databases, and required media
observation: A user saw about 180 to 190 GB and suspected duplicate Packs but did not trust Live's own search; replies warned that projects needed collected media and older libraries could remain.
product_implication: A duplicate claim must include content identity, reference reachability, owner version, and an open-project check.
quality_note: First-person report with mixed peer explanations. No prevalence or safe-delete rule is inferred.

title: External Storage and Backup
fact_scope: Ableton documents keeping the app and plug-ins on the system drive, maintaining system headroom, moving Packs and User Library through Live settings, configuring temporary recordings, and using Collect All and Save for referenced project media.
product_implication: Offer Live-owned relocation and project consolidation; preserve local working headroom and referenced media.
quality_note: First-party product documentation. It defines supported actions, not independent user demand.

title: Using third-party Packs
fact_scope: Ableton supports choosing a local or external folder for third-party Packs and notes that a Pack can contain presets, samples, and Live Sets.
product_implication: Treat a Pack as a compound owner object and route relocation through Live rather than moving child folders independently.
quality_note: First-party documentation. Third-party Pack behavior can vary by package.

title: The User Library
fact_scope: Ableton defines the User Library as custom presets, defaults, clips, templates, and collected samples, supports a custom external path, and provides owner-level management of unused samples.
product_implication: Classify the User Library as user-created owner data; expose Live's management tools instead of generic cache cleanup.
quality_note: First-party documentation. Owner-level unused-sample checks still need project-reference verification.

title: Ableton decoding-cache free-space and location rules
fact_scope: Ableton documents a configurable minimum-free-space threshold for the decoding cache and says the cache must be in a valid writable location in the same user profile.
product_implication: Explain configuration-based blockers before proposing deletion and show the owner setting that controls the threshold.
quality_note: First-party troubleshooting documentation. It applies to decoding errors, not every low-space case.

title: Ableton Live storage requirements
fact_scope: Ableton lists a modest app install, optional sound content up to tens of gigabytes, and system-drive headroom for temporary files and caching.
product_implication: Separate installed content, optional content, and runtime working space in the budget.
quality_note: First-party requirements that can change by Live version and platform.

title: Unreal's Derived Data Cache grew while projects lived elsewhere
observation: A developer stored resources on another drive but watched the system-drive DDC grow by about 9.5 GB in eleven days and initially removed unrelated apps to compensate.
product_implication: Attribute hidden growth to the owner, show that it is derived data, and estimate regeneration cost before cleanup.
quality_note: First-person report from an older Unreal version. Growth rate is not generalizable.

title: Low disk space appeared as a corrupt Unreal packaging cache
observation: The poster reported a cache-corruption error during Android packaging and said freeing system-drive space resolved it.
product_implication: Translate misleading owner errors into a storage hypothesis while preserving the build log and retry condition.
quality_note: Single first-person report. It supports diagnostic wording, not a universal error mapping.

title: Unreal filled the system drive despite an external project layout
observation: A developer said everything was on another drive while replies identified both DDC and launcher asset cache on the system drive.
product_implication: Map owner storage across project, engine, DDC, and asset-cache locations instead of assuming the project path explains total use.
quality_note: Forum troubleshooting across multiple Unreal versions; paths are version and platform sensitive.

title: Saving an Unreal project externally did not move all working data
observation: A user saved content to another drive but still lost 25 to 50 GB on the system drive and hit external-reference errors.
product_implication: Show project placement and owner working-data placement as separate budgets and repair paths.
quality_note: First-person report with peer guidance from an older Unreal version.

title: Unreal used about 82 GB across versions, cache, and autosaves
observation: During a version migration, a developer found large engine installs and a 36.49 GB user-area DDC; peers warned that autosaves should not be disabled without backup.
product_implication: Separate rebuildable cache from versions, assets, and recovery history; never trade recovery for space without explicit proof.
quality_note: First-person thread with mixed peer advice. Reported sizes are contextual.

title: Clearing the suggested Unreal cache did not fix the launch failure
observation: A user cleared the suggested cache but the launcher still failed, despite abundant disk space.
product_implication: Require post-action verification and keep a failed cleanup from becoming a success claim or repeated deletion loop.
quality_note: First-person counterexample. The root cause remained unresolved in the inspected passage.

title: Repeated Unreal lighting builds consumed hidden gigabytes
observation: An architecture user saw several gigabytes disappear with each lighting build outside the visible project folder; a reply linked growth to DDC and noted slower first open after deletion.
product_implication: Tie generated bytes to the action that created them and show active-project and regeneration cost.
quality_note: First-person report with peer attribution. Owner documentation is needed for exact scope.

title: A source build of Unreal reached about 170 GB
observation: A developer asked how to reduce a roughly 170 GB source build; replies distinguished rebuildable Intermediate and DDC data from the engine source and build result.
product_implication: Show artifact lineage, rebuild command, estimated time, and active branch before recommending source-build cleanup.
quality_note: First-person discussion from an older engine version; exact folder semantics require current owner docs.

title: Using Derived Data Cache in Unreal Engine
fact_scope: Epic documents local, shared, and cloud DDC layers, owner settings for moving local DDC, cleanup behavior, and a configuration that can duplicate local and shared caches for no gain.
product_implication: Use Unreal's configured DDC paths and retention rules; flag duplicate cache configuration before raw deletion.
quality_note: First-party current documentation. Configuration and defaults vary by engine version.

title: Set up Zen Storage Server as Shared DDC
fact_scope: Epic describes local, shared, and cloud cache layers, recommends a separate data drive to avoid making the system unusable, and ties capacity to team topology and latency.
product_implication: Do not treat team DDC as one user's junk; show ownership, service state, network role, and administrator handoff.
quality_note: First-party operational guidance. Shared-server actions are outside a local rescue scope without admin authority.

title: Derived Data settings in Unreal Engine
fact_scope: Unreal exposes recommended local and shared DDC configuration checks and warnings in project settings.
product_implication: Deep-link or hand off to the owner setting and verify that the configured path is active before cleanup.
quality_note: First-party reference. It documents settings, not deletion safety for every cache node.

title: Simulation Nodes caching and baking
fact_scope: Blender automatically caches simulation playback, supports baking to disk for rendering, allows per-modifier cache directories, and provides an owner action to delete cached or baked simulations.
product_implication: Mark simulation data as active project state and use Blender's delete action only after project and bake identity are clear.
quality_note: First-party development-version manual. Confirm behavior against the installed Blender release.

title: Baking physics simulations
fact_scope: Blender describes memory and disk caches, external paths, protected bakes, cache-step size trade-offs, and owner actions to delete bakes while noting time-consuming recomputation.
product_implication: Show exact scene ownership and recompute cost; hold active bakes and route cleanup through Blender.
quality_note: First-party Blender 5.0 manual. Physics systems can differ.

title: Blender render cache reached nearly a gigabyte per frame
observation: A peer reported BVH cache files near 1 GB per frame and said the system ran out of disk space during smoke work.
product_implication: Show per-frame growth and active render ownership before calling large generated folders safe to clear.
quality_note: Peer report in a troubleshooting thread from an older Blender version; the claim is directional.

title: A Blender user could not tell which fluid-cache layers were still needed
observation: After a resumable fluid bake produced more than 500 MB, the user asked whether intermediate cache could be removed while preserving the final result.
product_implication: Explain dependency layers and whether deletion invalidates resume, final output, or both; do not rank by age alone.
quality_note: First-person question with peer replies. Exact cache dependency is version-sensitive.

title: Removing Fusion exposed many residual folders on macOS
observation: A Mac user could not remove Fusion through normal UI and needed a long owner-provided list of app, cache, preference, and temporary locations.
product_implication: For app removal, separate application residue from user-created settings, tool libraries, and offline data, then use an owner uninstall path.
quality_note: First-person report with an Autodesk reply from an older version. Paths may have changed.

title: Fusion reported the same 13.94 GB blocker after free space rose to 60 GB
observation: A macOS user repeatedly saw the same update-space error while reported free space increased from about 30 GB to 60 GB; generic cleanup guidance did not explain the stale number.
product_implication: Name the measurement source and stale state; preserve failed attempts and avoid repeating broad cleanup without a changed blocker.
quality_note: First-person recent report with owner reply. The eventual cleanup did not isolate the root cause.

title: A long-running Fusion process drove about 135 GB of memory and disk pressure
observation: A user reported that leaving Fusion open for days led to about 135 GB of memory-related pressure and macOS freezing other apps.
product_implication: Treat live processes and swap pressure as active state; stop and diagnose the owner process before proposing filesystem deletion.
quality_note: Single recent first-person report. The split between physical memory and disk-backed swap was not measured.

title: Fusion placed more than 30 GB in a fixed user-profile cache
observation: A user found more than 30 GB of randomly named Fusion data and asked what was safe to delete; an owner reply said local cloud-synced cache could be reset but recommended the Fusion cleaner.
product_implication: Confirm cloud sync, offline state, personalization, and owner cleaner availability before reclaiming Fusion data.
quality_note: Older first-person thread with owner reply. Current offline behavior and paths need version checks.

title: Clearing Fusion caches and freeing space did not restore hub access
observation: The user freed substantial space, cleared multiple local caches, and reinstalled, but the hub-context failure remained and appeared account-side.
product_implication: A failed owner-cache reset must stop further cleanup and escalate with diagnostics; not every cache-shaped failure is local storage.
quality_note: First-person counterexample. It is adjacent because storage was not the root cause.

title: Fusion crash recovery risked personalized tool-library data
observation: A user wanted to preserve personalization settings and a tool library while owner support suggested renaming the offline-cache folder before relaunch.
product_implication: Before cache repair, identify user-created settings and tool libraries and preserve a recoverable copy with an owner-level relaunch test.
quality_note: First-person report with Autodesk support. It concerns repair safety as much as disk cleanup.

title: Fusion slowness was linked to cache file-system events
observation: After investigation, Autodesk linked slowness to file-system modification events around cache files and suggested owner cache clearing plus checking sync or security tools.
product_implication: Surface cache consumers and file watchers; cleanup alone may not fix the creation loop.
quality_note: Owner-supported diagnosis in a first-person thread. It is adjacent because the primary symptom was performance.

title: Deleting every visible Fusion folder did not fix a startup crash
observation: The user removed Autodesk application support, cache, and preference data, reinstalled, and even tried a new admin account, but the crash persisted.
product_implication: Do not repeat broader deletion after a clean owner-state test fails; preserve diagnostics and escalate the non-storage cause.
quality_note: First-person counterexample. It is adjacent because the storage cleanup did not address the failure.

title: About the Logic Pro and MainStage sound library on Mac
fact_scope: Logic 12 consolidates sounds into a library bundle; APFS can clone without extra space, other formats can require both old and new copies, interrupted cloning can resume, and old data should remain when older app versions still need it.
product_implication: Make filesystem format, version compatibility, transaction state, and copy verification prerequisites for reclaim.
quality_note: First-party current documentation. Behavior differs between Logic generations and file systems.

title: Consolidate project assets in Logic Pro
fact_scope: Logic's Consolidate command copies external audio, sampler data, video, loops, and other assets into the project so the project remains portable and complete.
product_implication: Offer consolidation before archive, move, or duplicate cleanup when project references cross storage locations.
quality_note: First-party user guide. Consolidation can increase bytes before it makes old locations reviewable.

title: Sound Library settings in Logic Pro
fact_scope: Logic 12 stores content in one library bundle, allows an internal, external, or network location, and provides Locate and Show in Finder controls when the library moves or is unavailable.
product_implication: Prefer the owner's Locate flow and record the resolved active bundle before presenting old copies.
quality_note: First-party current user guide.

title: Logic Pro technical storage requirements
fact_scope: Apple lists separate minimum-install and full-sound-library storage requirements for Logic Pro.
product_implication: Show base app, optional library, and temporary transaction budgets separately.
quality_note: First-party technical specifications that can change by release and locale.

title: Move Logic Pro and MainStage content
fact_scope: Apple documents supported moves, permission requirements, volume constraints, current Logic 12 bundle moves, and Retry, Ignore, or Reset behavior when a library volume is absent.
product_implication: Explain the consequences of owner choices and verify the destination before the original becomes reviewable.
quality_note: First-party current documentation; instructions branch by Logic version.

title: Install Logic sound content in smaller packages
fact_scope: Apple documents installing individual sound packages when the complete library cannot be downloaded at once and gives a current full-library size estimate.
product_implication: When the user needs content rather than cleanup, offer a smaller supported owner transaction and reserve a working-space buffer.
quality_note: First-party current troubleshooting guide; sizes can change.

title: Copy and move Logic Pro projects
fact_scope: Apple warns that Finder moves do not automatically include externally referenced project assets and points users to owner-level asset management first.
product_implication: A moved project is not verified until external references are consolidated or tested; do not infer safety from a successful filesystem copy.
quality_note: First-party guide for an older Logic branch, but the reference-boundary principle remains relevant and should be version-checked.

title: Manage and delete Logic sound packs
fact_scope: Logic 12 shows pack sizes and provides owner-level download, update, and delete actions while keeping the library in one bundle that can be relocated.
product_implication: Use pack-level owner actions and show future redownload cost rather than deleting inside the bundle.
quality_note: First-party current user guide.
